 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Karen Khachanov has decided to part ways with his long-time coach Vedran Martic. 
 Khachanov just took part in the Shanghai Masters, where he knocked out Arthur Fery and Adrian Mannarino before losing to Alex de Minaur in the last 16. The Russian quickly moves on to the Almaty Open, with the fifth seed starting out in round one against qualifier Rei Sakamoto.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But the seven-time ATP champion will be without Martic at the ATP 250 tournament in Kazakhstan following their split, which the current world number 25 has just confirmed on his social media.
 Karen Khachanov confirms split with Vedran Martic
 Posting an emotional message on his Instagram, former ATP number eight Khachanov wrote: "Vedran and I have mutually decided to bring our professional partnership to an end after nearly 10 years of working together in total.
 "Vedran has been my coach since the very beginning of my career. I came to Split to work with him when I was just 15 and a half years old. Throughout this entire journey, he has always supported me, and we have achieved so much together: breaking into the Top 10, winning titles, and growing tremendously along the way.

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "To me, Vedran is much more than just a coach. He is a true friend and someone very close to my heart, someone who will always feel like family. He dedicated himself wholeheartedly to our work together, taught me so much, and I am incredibly grateful to him for everything.
 "We are parting ways as player and coach, but this is not goodbye. Thank you for everything, Vedran! You may no longer be my coach, but you will always be family."
 Almaty may be a difficult tournament for Khachanov given his significant decision, but he has little time to ponder the move. The 30-year-old certainly doesn't have an easy potential run in Kazakhstan, where he could face Tomas Machac should he make it past Sakamoto.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After that, the Russian could be drawn against home favourite Alexander Bublik in the quarterfinals. His compatriot Daniil Medvedev represents a possible semifinal opponent in Almaty, where a final against one of Andrey Rublev, Stefanos Tsitsipas or Luciano Darderi is on the cards. He does, however, know what it takes to win the event, having lifted the trophy in 2024.
